newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: E.Europe share indices rise despite foreign apathy.
newsitem.headline: E.Europe share indices rise despite foreign apathy.

text.p: By Robin Shepherd,
Most central and eastern European share indices posted moderate gains this week but analysts said the region was still affected by a lack of interest from international investors.

Foreign buyers were most notably absent from Prague and Bratislava, while Warsaw recovered from heavy falls in the previous week and Bucharest saw a near doubling of trade turnover, led by increased interest in major issues.
Despite gains to all the main markets, the Central European Share Index (CESI) of 73 selected Czech, Polish, Hungarian, Slovak and Slovenian stocks fell by two percent on the week to 1,503.56 points.
PRAGUE
Czech shares showed the first signs of a turnaround in the second half of the week, raising hopes among local dealers that the long sustained bear run in Czech equities may be coming to an end.
However, dealers warned against premature optimism, saying activity was too low to draw firm conclusions about the direction of the market.
"The volumes are thin and there's very low foreign participation. It goes back to the same old problem of thinness on the market," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.
WARSAW
Polish shares rose 3.8 percent this week after last week's 6.1 percent fall and analysts said the market would probably begin to stabilise.

"I don't see any signal which would mobilise demand," said Dariusz Szepieniec of Bank Slaski brokerage, adding though that the market might still have some upward potential in the near term after last week's steep fall.
Analysts said the threat of further falls on foreign bourses over concerns that interest rates may rise could continue to slow buying in Warsaw as well.
BUDAPEST
The BUX index on the Hungarian stock market gained more than three percent through the week, pushed by a stronger dollar.

The dollar's continued strengthening, in addition to the monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate of the forint against the central bank's currency basket, makes Hungarian stocks cheaper for foreign investors.
The Hungarian bourse is suffering from a dearth of domestic information as it awaits first quarter earnings reports and planned share issues.
BRATISLAVA
The Slovak bourse again traded very small volumes this week with brokers seeing little chance of an upturn while interest from foreign investors remains so low.
The official 16-share SAX index fell 1.74 percent.
"We expect the sluggish trading to remain in coming days as foreign investors show little interest in starting more active trading in our market," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Sykora said the SAX should hover around its current levels, or decline slightly next week.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks started the week slowly ahead of municipal elections on Sunday but good 1996 company results pushed prices higher in mid-week and traders saw the trend continuing.
In the absence of foreign investors, scared away by the poll, local traders dominated buying and many were betting that the elections would not affect economic policy.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares rose 1.32 percent this week.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC was the biggest gainer, jumping 10.9 percent. The preferred shares of Hipotekarna Banka Brezice led the decliners, tumbling 18.9 percent.

Traders said stagnation on the market will continue until foreign capital returns as domestic investors do not have enough money to support constant growth on the market which expects new listings next month.
The central bank demanded that international portfolio investors open custody accounts at Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade shares.
BUCHAREST

Investor interest in Romanian stocks picked up this week with the Bucharest bourse seeing large volumes. Turnover was almost double at 15.9 billion lei against last week's 9.0 billion with most prices moving higher on strong demand.

Dealers said active trading during the week reflected investors' focus on the first-tier high-caps ahead of 1996 financial results, which might boost their prices. APRIL 11 CLOSE WEEK'S CHANGE 1997 HIGH 1997 LOW
